extraction_metadata.source_type: peer-reviewed journal article + open companion database
extraction_metadata.notes: Extracted from the Nature Biotechnology article and the companion CicciaLab DDR Genetic Interactions Database. This extraction is the keystone reference for the AISciMShub Phase 1 DDR-Neuro bridge — the article's architectural pattern (combinatorial perturbation of a coherent gene set, published as an open queryable map) is what the platform is porting to neuroprotection.

title: Cas12a-Based Combinatorial Knockout Screens Define the Genetic Architecture of the DNA Damage Response
subtitle_or_tagline: From single-gene stories to network stories: a 233-gene pairwise knockout map with >750 high-confidence genetic interactions and 2,029 AlphaFold-multimer physical rationalizations.
topic: The authors used a Cas12a-based CRISPR knockout system to combinatorially perturb 233 DNA damage response (DDR) genes — both individually and in 27,028 pairwise combinations — across MCF10A and TP53-deleted RPE-1 cell lines. The GRAPE pipeline quantified pairwise fitness effects, yielding >750 high-confidence genetic interactions (FDR < 0.1) spanning synthetic lethal (negative) and buffering (positive) relationships. AlphaFold-Multimer predictions for 2,029 gene pairs physically rationalize the genetic interactions. The full interaction map was released as an open queryable database, establishing the canonical reference for DDR network biology.

components: Cas12a CRISPR knockout library targeting 233 DDR genes (699 single-gene constructs, 27,028 pairwise constructs, 81,084 total constructs)
Two cell-line contexts: MCF10A (non-tumorigenic breast epithelial) and RPE-1 (retinal pigment epithelial, TP53-deleted)
GRAPE pipeline (Traver Hart Lab) for pairwise fitness scoring with local variance normalization
AlphaFold-Multimer physical interaction prediction for top-scoring gene pairs
Open companion database (ddr-genetic-interactions.ciccialab-database.com) with heatmap visualization and CSV export
architecture.data_flow: Cas12a library design → lentiviral transduction → pooled growth under unperturbed conditions → early (T9) + final (T17/T18) sequencing time points → GRAPE fitness estimation → pairwise genetic interaction z-scores → FDR thresholding → module clustering → AlphaFold-Multimer structural prediction → public database release
input_types: curated 233-gene DDR gene set (Fanconi anemia, HR, NER, NHEJ, MMR, TLS, replication fork, checkpoint)
Cas12a guide RNA library (single + pairwise constructs)
Illumina sequencing reads at T0, T9, T17/T18
output_types: pairwise genetic interaction z-scores (negative = synthetic lethal, positive = buffering)
functional module assignments (46-69 modules per dataset)
AlphaFold-Multimer physical interaction predictions for 2,029 pairs
open queryable web database with heatmap + CSV export

workflow_steps: Step 1 - Curate the 233-gene DDR set spanning Fanconi anemia, homologous recombination, NER, NHEJ, mismatch repair, translesion synthesis, replication fork protection, and checkpoint pathways.
Step 2 - Design a Cas12a combinatorial knockout library: 699 single-gene constructs + 27,028 pairwise constructs (81,084 total guide RNAs).
Step 3 - Transduce MCF10A and TP53-deleted RPE-1 cells, grow under unperturbed conditions, and sequence at early (T9) and final (T17/T18) time points.
Step 4 - Apply the GRAPE pipeline: estimate single-mutant fitness, expected double-knockout fitness under additivity, and apply local variance normalization to produce genetic interaction z-scores.
Step 5 - Threshold at FDR < 0.1 to define >750 high-confidence interactions; cluster into 46-69 functional modules per dataset.
Step 6 - Run AlphaFold-Multimer on top-scoring pairs to physically rationalize the genetic interactions (2,029 modeled pairs).
Step 7 - Release the full interaction map as an open queryable database with heatmap visualization, CSV export, and AlphaFold confidence annotations.
key_claims: The 233 DDR genes were screened in 27,028 pairwise combinations, yielding >750 high-confidence genetic interactions at FDR < 0.1 — the first genome-scale open interaction map for the DDR.
Synthetic lethal interactions were identified between the REV1-Pol ζ translesion polymerase complex and the MCM8-MCM9-HROB helicase complex, linking translesion synthesis to mitotic DNA repair.
Buffering (positive) interactions between Fanconi anemia genes and mitotic DNA repair genes reveal functional redundancy that explains resistance to single-pathway therapeutic targeting.
Synthetic lethal interactions between SMARCAL1 (replication fork remodeler) and FANCM complex components connect replication stress response to Fanconi anemia.

AlphaFold-Multimer predictions for 2,029 gene pairs provide physical rationalization: many synthetic lethal pairs do NOT physically interact, indicating parallel-pathway rather than direct-complex compensation.
Functional module clustering (46-69 modules per dataset) redefines DDR pathway boundaries beyond the textbook HR/NER/NHEJ/NHEJ/TLS division.
The open companion database establishes a canonical reference: any subsequent DDR paper will cite it, and any DDR drug discovery program will query it.
caveats_or_warnings: The screen was run in MCF10A and TP53-deleted RPE-1 cell lines — both dividing, non-neuronal contexts. The genetic interaction architecture may differ in post-mitotic neurons.
Cas12a knockout efficiency varies across genomic contexts; low-efficiency perturbations can produce false negatives.
Genetic interactions are context-dependent: a synthetic lethal pair in MCF10A may be buffered in RPE-1, and vice versa. The map is a starting point, not a universal truth.
AlphaFold-Multimer predictions are structural hypotheses, not experimental validations of physical interaction.
The companion database does not state an explicit open-data license (copyright Ciccia Lab, Columbia University). Reuse beyond querying the web interface requires contacting the lab.

bridge_relevance.role: keystone source article for AISciMShub Phase 1 (DDR-Neuro bridge) and Phase 3 (Neuroprotection Genetic Interaction Map)
bridge_relevance.methodology_port: The Cas12a combinatorial knockout + GRAPE scoring + open database pattern is directly portable to a 200-250 gene neuroprotection-relevant set (see build plan Chapter 3).
bridge_relevance.database_template: The CicciaLab database architecture (gene A × gene B → interaction score, effect size, AlphaFold confidence) is the template for the planned Neuro-SLI matrix and the Compound × Pathway × Vulnerability triangle database.
bridge_relevance.asymmetric_opportunity: The DDR field discovered synthetic lethal interactions among human genes but did not connect them to the chemical space of compounds that could exploit them. AISciMShub holds the compound side; adding the genetic interaction side completes a triangle no one else has.
